verdict.reasoning: Patient reports soreness and cracked skin on hands, mainly palms: 'I have uh soreness in my fingers, ... the skin on my hands is kind of cracked' and 'the palm... it's very, it's very bad in my hands.'

'A couple of months ago. I got it three, four months ago.' supports 3–4 months duration, but there is no statement that pain increased specifically 'in the last few weeks.' That timing of worsening is not mentioned.
Intermittent itch and bleeding only when scratched are described: 'it's itchy. Not all the time' and 'when I scratched it, yes it has bled sometimes but… it hasn't bled on its own.'
Patient states inability to work for past 3 days: 'the past three days, I haven't been able to go to work.'

She is a hotel housekeeper with inconsistent glove use and chemical exposure: 'I do work as a housekeeper… I'm not always very good about wearing gloves… At a hotel. I have to do the whole thing like bedrooms, bathrooms' and doctor links this: 'there's definitely, maybe a correlation between the two.'

ROS negatives and appetite are documented: 'Any other symptoms, such as fever…? Patient: No. Any nausea, or any vomiting? Patient: No. Any problem with your bowels? Patient: No. Any problem with your urine…? Patient: No.' and 'your appetite is well-maintained? Patient: Yeah.'
History of type 2 diabetes is explicit: 'I have diabetes.' / 'Do you know if that's type one or type two? Patient: Type two.'
Metformin use is stated: 'Which medications do you take?... Doctor: Metformin, OK.'
OTC E45 cream use: 'have you tried anything… any creams? Patient: Yeah. I tried uh E forty five.'
Antihistamine with no benefit: 'I also tried an antihistamine… but it didn't' and earlier 'Yeah, no it didn't really do anything' re: E45/attempted treatments.
No known allergies: 'Do you have any allergies, either to any medications or in general? Patient: No.'
Family history of diabetes: 'Family history-wise… Patient: Diabetes and what? Doctor: Diabetes as well. OK.'
Social history: 'I do work as a housekeeper' and 'At a hotel'; 'Do you smoke at all? Patient: No.'; alcohol: 'a couple of pints a week… very minimal, alcohol there.'

Doctor’s assessment: 'you might have something called dermatitis or contact dermatitis… people in your field, who are using cleaning products, not using gloves…' along with symptoms of dryness, cracking, pain, and itchiness on palms described earlier.
While T2DM and metformin use are documented, there is no statement that diabetes is 'stable' or about its current control: 'I have diabetes… Type two… Metformin, OK.'
Doctor advises avoiding triggers and strict glove use: 'we try and do is, you know, avoid the triggers. In your case, I strongly recommend that you wear gloves when cleaning at all times.'

Plan mentions steroid cream and stronger emollients but not potency level or exact frequency of 'four times daily for 2 weeks': 'we can try some steroid creams… as well as some stronger emollients… three four times a day, for the next couple of weeks.' The specific 'moderate-potency' label is not stated.
Education on frequent emollient use: 'stronger emollients, um which you really need to kind of coat on, three four times a day, for the next couple of weeks.'
There is no explicit instruction to continue metformin or mention of routine diabetes follow-up in the plan; diabetes management is not discussed beyond history and medication listing.

Follow-up instructions: 'if it still hasn't got better in about a week, two weeks time, I really need you to come back and see me again' and later 'minimum couple of weeks. Uh ten days to fourteen days. Um and if it still hasn't got better, or indeed if it's getting worse… come back and see me sooner.'
